description: One plain-English story line per ATT&CK tactic shortname, all three domains (Phase 14a). Keyed by tactic shortname because shortnames are shared across domains while TA-ids are not. Hand-written once — never generated at runtime. Completeness against attack.json is test-enforced (test_mitre_plain_language.py).

tactics.reconnaissance: researching the target before the attack — gathering names, systems, and weaknesses
tactics.resource-development: setting up attack infrastructure — buying domains, building malware, and staging accounts for later use
tactics.initial-access: how attackers first get in — phishing, exposed services, or stolen logins
tactics.execution: how attackers run their code on your systems
tactics.persistence: how attackers make sure they survive reboots and stay in
tactics.privilege-escalation: how attackers turn a normal foothold into admin-level control
tactics.stealth: how attackers hide — disguising files, wiping traces, and blending into normal activity
tactics.defense-impairment: how attackers switch off your defenses — disabling antivirus, EDR, and logging
tactics.defense-evasion: how attackers avoid being noticed on the device — hiding, disguising, and dodging analysis
tactics.credential-access: how attackers steal passwords, hashes, and tokens
tactics.discovery: how attackers look around — mapping accounts, systems, and networks once inside
tactics.lateral-movement: how attackers spread between systems once inside
tactics.collection: how attackers gather the data they are after
tactics.command-and-control: how the attacker's foothold phones home for instructions
tactics.exfiltration: how stolen data actually leaves your network
tactics.impact: the damage phase — encrypting, destroying, or disrupting systems and data
tactics.evasion: how attackers avoid detection inside industrial control systems
tactics.inhibit-response-function: stopping safety and protection systems from responding when the industrial process goes wrong
tactics.impair-process-control: manipulating the industrial process itself — changing what the plant actually does
tactics.network-effects: intercepting or manipulating a mobile device's network traffic
tactics.remote-service-effects: abusing cloud services connected to a mobile device (locate, wipe, backup) against its owner
